question.knowledge_point: Calculating the Intersection of a Circle With the X-Axis
question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13959190/assets/c6d356b443128da569a6b60065769cdb56e2e0059db7b146a3c4035d18a32228.png)

Find the $x$-intercepts of the circle $(x-1)^{2}+(y-3)^{2}=45,$ shown above.
question.worked_solution:
We must have $y=0$ at the $x$-intercepts. 

So, we need to substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the circle and solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-1)^{2}+(y-3)^{2} & =45 \\ (x-1)^{2}+(0-3)^{2} & =45 \\ (x-1)^{2}+9 & =45 \\ (x-1)^{2} & =36 \\ x-1 & =\pm \sqrt{36} \\ x & =1\pm 6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $x$-intercepts occur at the points $(-5,0)$ and $(7,0).$

evidence.solution_quote: Therefore, the $x$-intercepts occur at the points $(-5,0)$ and $(7,0).$
